name: missing_dependency
description: A necessary premise, dependency edge, or intermediate support is omitted, so a later conclusion is used without enough support.
example: Use AM-GM without depending on positivity of the variables.

name: wrong_theorem
description: A theorem, lemma, or named rule is replaced by a similar but invalid rule.
example: Use AAA as if it proved triangle congruence.

name: wrong_dependency
description: A proof step depends on an irrelevant, unknown, or logically insufficient earlier step.
example: Derive a divisibility claim from an unrelated parity observation.

name: false_claim
description: A false or unsupported intermediate claim is inserted and then used as if it were proved.
example: Assert that every three consecutive integers have product divisible by 12.

name: missing_case
description: One necessary branch of a case split is omitted while the proof proceeds as if all cases were covered.
example: Treat only the even case and forget the odd case.

name: sign_error
description: An algebraic sign, inequality direction, or arithmetic relation is changed incorrectly.
example: Change x-y into x+y, or change <= into >=.

name: invalid_wlog
description: A without-loss-of-generality reduction is made without a valid symmetry or coverage argument.
example: Assume a>=b>=c even though the expression is not symmetric.

name: circular_reasoning
description: A step directly or indirectly depends on the final conclusion it is supposed to prove.
example: Use the desired conclusion as a premise for an intermediate lemma.

name: overgeneralization
description: A statement proved in a special situation is applied to all cases.
example: Use a result shown for odd n as if it held for every n.

name: domain_error
description: A theorem or expression is used outside its valid domain.
example: Divide by a quantity that might be zero, or apply AM-GM to nonpositive terms.

name: quantifier_error
description: A statement about all objects is weakened to some objects, or an existence statement is used as universal.
example: Use a property that holds for one constructed point as if it held for every point.

name: unproved_existence
description: An object or parameter is introduced and used without proving it exists.
example: Choose an intersection point without proving the two lines intersect.

name: case_overlap
description: The proof uses cases that overlap or fail to partition all possibilities cleanly.
example: Split into n even and n prime, which are neither disjoint nor exhaustive.

name: diagram_assumption
description: A geometric relation suggested by a diagram is assumed without proof.
example: Assume two lines are parallel because they look parallel.
